text:
The talk around Sidney Crosby this week isn't about his game. It's about whether the unthinkable is thinkable: TribLIVE's Mark Madden asked exactly that, and other outlets have run with trade chatter around a Penguins team that keeps losing. Nothing in our facts says Crosby wants out, and he has played 1,439 games in one sweater. But that's the conversation.

On the ice, he's been fine rather than vintage. Thirteen points in 19 games, 19:32 a night, and the Penguins have had 52% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there. His own chances are slightly ahead of his goals, so the finishing isn't the problem. The setup game is still elite: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile among forwards for primary shot assists last season.

Our talent range puts his scoring rate well above what he's showing now. If his linemates start converting what he creates, the points follow. Whether that happens in Pittsburgh is the story to watch.
headline: Crosby, 39, and the questions in Pittsburgh
